> A comment for https://github.com/gufo-org/gufo/issues/475, replying to the maintainer's answer of 7 Oct 2026. Not posted:
> the owner sends it. Everything below this note is meant to be pasted as written; every link in it is absolute and live.

Thanks, that's a useful answer, and quick.

I think the change you mean is https://github.com/gufo-org/gufo/pull/282 (use official text-model defaults, merged 28 Sep, between the two builds we compared); #332 is the greedy-penalty performance one. Its description says requests that omitted sampling options used greedy defaults, with request > CLI > model precedence. That would explain higher acceptance on the older build.

One thing I want to check, because we don't rely on server defaults. Our launcher passes the same flags to both builds, and has done since before either run:

```
--think on --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
```

and the client sends no sampling fields of its own. On 0.5.0 the startup line confirms it took effect: `[sampling] event=defaults thinking=on temperature=1 top_k=20 top_p=0.95 min_p=0`. The older build printed no sampling line, so I can't see from our side what it applied.

So the question: on the build before #282, did those CLI flags apply to chat requests that omitted sampling fields, or did the server stay greedy for them regardless?

- If they were ignored, then we ran greedy before and sampled after, and the whole gap is the effect you describe. Nothing to fix, and it tells us our earlier runs were greedy.
- If they applied, both builds sampled identically for us, and something else is lowering acceptance. In that case the numbers in the issue stand.

Either answer is useful. Thanks for the pointer to the latest release too; we pin by digest and compare series, so moving starts a new one, but we'll look.
